About this page

A studio project by Claudio Cabana and Harper Sherman. The Pacific Design Institute is hypothetical; the project is used here to show what an Engage Kit tool looks like. Nothing you enter leaves this device.

From the design team, written for this page
In the design team’s words

Building in a Plaza

The project is organized around a large hardscaped public plaza in the heart of Mount Pleasant, accessed from the nearby SkyTrain station through Main Alley. Its compact massing establishes a strong urban edge along Quebec Street, activating the ground floor with rentable studio spaces. Two material identities mediate between the building's public and private roles.

The exterior façade is expressed in precast bio-char concrete, with large shingled panels forming a quiet backdrop for public life. The building relies on natural ventilation, using the concrete panels to regulate interior temperatures. Inside, the material language shifts to locally sourced timber structure, creating an atmosphere of warmth and quiet concentration that supports the rhythms of daily work.

From the presentation poster

The institute

PDI is an interdisciplinary research collaborative focused exclusively on the advancement of regional building solutions. Through diverse faculty expertise, cutting-edge facilities, and dynamic partnerships with manufacturers, designers, and other stakeholders, PDI oversees a wide range of testing and applied research and provides unique educational opportunities for a growing workforce.
